_comment: Hand-written editorial notes about the XR_DXR_* extensions — the ONLY place
they are maintained. The extension SET is derived from the headers in
which hard-fails when a header has no entry here (or an entry names no
header). That is what stops the published surfaces from drifting: the
displayxr-extensions README, its machine-readable extensions.json, and the
displayxr.org/extensions page are all generated or merged from this file.
Adding a header without a note here fails the `lint` workflow.
'summary' is one sentence, README-length. Longer prose for the website
lives in displayxr-website/app/extensions/page.tsx and is merged by name;
where none exists the website falls back to this summary, so an extension
can never be missing from the public list.

groups.title: Display capability
groups.blurb: What the runtime tells apps about the 3D display they are rendering on.

groups.title: Rendering, projection & compositing
groups.blurb: How an app drives the runtime's view math, declares which regions of its window are 3D, and hands pre-weave content to the vendor display processor — instead of re-implementing projection or weaving itself.

groups.title: App window binding
groups.blurb: How an app hands its native window to the runtime so the compositor can output into it.

groups.title: Workspace controller surface
groups.blurb: The contract that lets a workspace controller — the DisplayXR Shell, or any third-party / OEM / vertical / AI-agent equivalent — drive the spatial-desktop layer on top of the runtime. Activation is gated by orchestrator-PID match; the runtime trusts whatever binary it was configured to spawn.

groups.title: Agent control
groups.blurb: How applications plug into the AI-agent surface, exposing their own actions through the same MCP framework the runtime and workspace controllers use.

groups.title: Capture
groups.blurb: Getting the composed multi-view frame back out of the runtime — for screenshots, recording, and dataset generation.

XR_DXR_display_info.title: Display Info
XR_DXR_display_info.summary: Display dimensions, eye-tracking modes, and the data needed for asymmetric (Kooima) projection

XR_DXR_view_rig.title: View Rig
XR_DXR_view_rig.summary: App declares a display or camera rig descriptor and consumes render-ready XrView{pose, fov}; the runtime owns the projection math

XR_DXR_display_zones.title: Display Zones
XR_DXR_display_zones.summary: A layout of independent 3D zones and flat 2D zones across one display, each 3D zone with its own view rig, plus the wish mask a switchable-lens panel honours

XR_DXR_local_3d_zone.title: Local 3D Zones
XR_DXR_local_3d_zone.summary: Per-pixel 3D-ness mask over an app's own window, with the flat 2D side as a first-class post-weave composition layer

XR_DXR_depth_budget.title: Rear Depth Budget
XR_DXR_depth_budget.summary: Advisory limit on how far behind the display plane a transparent app may render, chained on XrViewState at xrLocateViews

XR_DXR_weave.title: Window Weave Service
XR_DXR_weave.summary: Window-bound synchronous weave for present-owners: hand the runtime a stereo texture and a window rect, get back a weaved shared texture and a fence

XR_DXR_win32_window_binding.title: Win32 Window Binding
XR_DXR_win32_window_binding.summary: App-provided HWND, shared texture, canvas sub-rect

XR_DXR_xlib_window_binding.title: Xlib Window Binding
XR_DXR_xlib_window_binding.summary: App-provided X11 Display* and Window (desktop Linux)

XR_DXR_android_surface_binding.title: Android Surface Binding
XR_DXR_android_surface_binding.summary: App-provided Android Surface / ANativeWindow, republished across background and resume, with the per-frame window rect

XR_DXR_spatial_workspace.title: Spatial Workspace
XR_DXR_spatial_workspace.summary: Multi-app composition: window pose, hit-test, capture, overlay, modal input grab

XR_DXR_workspace_file_dialog.title: Workspace File Dialog
XR_DXR_workspace_file_dialog.summary: Async spatial-native file picker spawned by the active workspace controller, with fallback to the platform dialog

XR_DXR_mcp_tools.title: App MCP Tools
XR_DXR_mcp_tools.summary: An app registers its own MCP tools with the runtime's agent surface; calls arrive on the OpenXR event queue

XR_DXR_atlas_capture.title: Atlas Capture
XR_DXR_atlas_capture.summary: Vendor-neutral PNG snapshot of the multi-view atlas at a caller-selected compositor stage, for any app class
